Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

practice noun

custom, the usual way

also custom, habit, usual practice, common practice, way of doing things, as is the custom, convention (a custom), social convention, routine, daily routine, the usual routine

classical

Catull. 9.8: ut mōs est tuus
Aug. Conf. 9.7.15: secundum mōrem orientālium partium

mōs, mōris m.

noun, third declension

custom, practice, way

mōs est, it is the custom; ut mōs est, as usual. The plural mōrēs is a person’s ways or character.

Other words

  • cōnsuētūdō, cōnsuētūdinis f. — habit, usage

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.2.8: fit ex hīs cōnsuētūdō, inde nātūra; Cic. Att. 4.17.1: oblītum cōnsuētūdinis et īnstitūtī meī

    A habit formed by doing something often.

  • īnstitūtum, īnstitūtī n. — established practice; one’s custom

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.17.1: cōnsuētūdinis et īnstitūtī meī

    What someone has made a rule of doing, or what has been established.

Examples

  • vīsam tē incolumem audiamque Hibērum narrantem loca, facta, nātiōnēs, ut mōs est tuus

    I shall see you safe and sound and hear you tell of the places, the doings and the peoples of Spain, as is your wayCatull. 9.6–8

  • putō tē exīstimāre mē nunc oblītum cōnsuētūdinis et īnstitūtī meī rārius ad tē scrībere quam solēbam

    I suppose you think that I have now forgotten my habit and my usual practice, and write to you less often than I used toCic. Att. 4.17.1

  • fit ex hīs cōnsuētūdō, inde nātūra

    from these comes habit, and from habit, natureQuint. 1.2.8

See also practice, as usual.
